html:
Jorge Eliécer Gaitán was a Colombian Liberal politician and orator, mayor of Bogotá and the most popular leader of his time. His murder on 9 April 1948 set off the Bogotazo.

From a modest family, he studied law in Bogotá and Rome. He became famous in 1929 for his speeches in Congress on the banana massacre. He attacked the oligarchy of both parties and promised land and rights to workers and peasants, drawing huge crowds. In 1947 he took control of the Liberal Party.

His killer was lynched, and who was behind the murder has never been proven. Many Colombians believe that his death took away the chance of peaceful reform and led to La Violencia and the later wars of Colombia.
sum: Jorge Eliécer Gaitán was a Colombian Liberal politician and orator, mayor of Bogotá and the most popular leader of his time. His murder on 9 April 1948 set off the Bogotazo.
